source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 205: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: the hang is reproducible during process-group/NCCL initialization, the launcher can collect per-rank logs, and no platform, driver, or network detail is known until measured. Treat all timings and topology claims as measurements, not facts.

Hypothesis: one or more ranks have inconsistent world size/rank assignment, rendezvous identity, or selected interface/address, so the expected collective membership cannot be formed; a secondary hypothesis is a topology, GPU-visibility, or transport-path fault. Falsification requires every rank to report the same job/attempt identifier, world size, rank, local rank, device UUID, rendezvous endpoint, and collective sequence, plus a successful minimal all-reduce with the same configuration.

1. Capture a timestamped, redacted manifest: launcher arguments, software/driver versions, hostnames, rank and local-rank mapping, CUDA-visible devices/UUIDs, GPU count, topology, container limits, ulimits, CPU/memory state, rendezvous/store endpoint, selected interface and resolved addresses, and NCCL/debug logs. Verify authorization before exposing logs and remove tokens, private addresses, and other secrets.
2. Check that all expected ranks joined exactly once, agree on world size and rendezvous identity, resolve/reach the store through the intended path, and enter collectives in identical order. Compare the first missing rank and last completed event rather than relying on a single aggregate timeout. Check GPU visibility and device uniqueness per rank, then inspect peer/topology paths and container/network namespace boundaries.
3. Run a minimal deterministic all-reduce with a small tensor and checksum, first on one node, then on a reduced world, then on the full world. Keep launcher, software, environment, rank mapping, timeout, and retry policy matched; randomize run order and repeat enough times to distinguish intermittent failures. Test the explicitly selected interface/path only in an authorized, reversible configuration. Use a bounded watchdog, collect diagnostics on timeout, terminate children, and clean up the store; do not repeatedly retry an unhealthy production job.

Measure for each attempt: rendezvous/join and collective completion times (median and p95/p99), success and timeout/hang counts, failing rank and phase, all-reduce checksum/correctness, selected transport/interface, GPU and host utilization, memory, and cleanup success. A single-node pass but reduced/full-world failure supports a cross-host membership or transport issue; a reduced-world failure narrows it to the participating ranks; checksum failure is distinct from a hang. Confounders include changing rank placement, stale stores, concurrent jobs, firewall/MTU or DNS changes, topology asymmetry, GPU reset state, driver/library mismatch, resource pressure, and altered timeout behavior.

Rollback criteria: stop experiments and restore the previous launcher, interface, timeout, and environment if correctness fails, error rates or tail latency regress materially, unauthorized data appears, or watchdog cleanup is incomplete. Preserve immutable manifests and logs for expert review. Evidence required before a root-cause claim: per-rank manifests/logs, rendezvous and collective timelines, topology/device checks, matched single/reduced/full-world results with repetitions, checksums, and cleanup records. This is a provisional diagnosis plan, not proof of a particular NCCL or network fault.
risks: A timeout can hide whether the cause is rendezvous, collective-order, topology, or transport failure.
Changing interface, timeout, rank placement, or retries can confound comparisons or worsen an unhealthy job.
Logs and network manifests may contain credentials, private addresses, or sensitive topology details.
evidence_required: Redacted per-rank environment, rank/world-size and rendezvous records; topology/GPU visibility and interface/path evidence; matched repeated single-node, reduced-world, and full-world minimal all-reduce results with checksums and latency distributions; timeout, failing-phase, and cleanup logs.

Verify authorization before exposing logs and remove tokens, private addresses, and other secrets.
2. Check that all expected ranks joined exactly once, agree on world size and rendezvous identity, resolve/reach the store through the intended path, and enter collectives in identical order. Compare the first missing rank and last completed event rather than relying on a single aggregate timeout. Check GPU visibility and device uniqueness per rank, then inspect peer/topology paths and container/network namespace boundaries.
3. Run a minimal deterministic all-reduce with a small tensor and checksum, first on one node, then on a reduced world, then on the full world. Keep launcher, software, environment, rank mapping, timeout, and retry policy matched; randomize run order and repeat enough times to distinguish intermittent failures. Test the explicitly selected interface/path only in an authorized, reversible configuration. Use a bounded watchdog, collect diagnostics on timeout, terminate children, and clean up the store; do not repeatedly retry an unhealthy production job.

Measure for each attempt: rendezvous/join and collective completion times (median and p95/p99), success and timeout/hang counts, failing rank and phase, all-reduce checksum/correctness, selected transport/interface, GPU and host utilization, memory, and cleanup success. Confounders include changing rank placement, stale stores, concurrent jobs, firewall/MTU or DNS changes, topology asymmetry, GPU reset state, driver/library mismatch, resource pressure, and altered timeout behavior.

Rollback criteria: stop experiments and restore the previous launcher, interface, timeout, and environment if correctness fails, error rates or tail latency regress materially, unauthorized data appears, or watchdog cleanup is incomplete. Preserve immutable manifests and logs for expert review. Evidence required before a root-cause claim: per-rank manifests/logs, rendezvous and collective timelines, topology/device checks, matched single/reduced/full-world results with repetitions, checksums, and cleanup records. This is a provisional diagnosis plan, not proof of a particular NCCL or network fault.
